title: Localisation of the pilonidal sinus and postoperative wound healing: a prospective observational study
summary:
Pilonidal sinus is an inflammatory condition in the gluteal cleft that primarily affects young adults. Typical symptoms include pain, discharge of fluid or blood, and abscesses. This chronic condition is usually treated with surgery. 

If minimally invasive methods are not suitable for the condition, established surgical procedures include the Karydakis plasty and the Cleft Lift operation.  Despite good treatment outcomes, wound healing complications may occur after surgery. These usually resolve without the need for further surgery, but in some cases may require additional treatment.

It is currently unclear whether the location of the pilonidal sinus influences the risk of wound healing complications. Particularly in patients who have undergone previous surgery, the lesion extends ever closer to the anus. This study therefore aims to investigate whether a short distance between the lesion and the anal margin is associated with an increased risk of postoperative wound healing complications.

interventions.name: Patients with pilonidal sinus who undergo surgery using the Karydakis procedure or the Cleft Lift technique.
